scoring_limits: K1: Strong official city population, general mobility and sustainability-attitude evidence plus a method-labelled national climate survey. No independently measured Amsterdam taxi/ride-hailing trip volume, user frequency, price elasticity or willingness to pay for EV taxis. Municipal mode split is about residents’ travel, not all travel inside the city; no taxi category is separated. National climate attitudes cannot be presented as the selected segment’s actual preference.

K1 date correction: the municipal synthesis is dated February 2026, but mobility data are 2023 and climate intention survey is March 2023 (n=1,660). The 2022 climate-concern statement has a different survey base. Do not label all these data 2026 observations.

K2: National ILT figures establish taxi SUPPLY (41,356 vehicles in 2025; 59,094 cards and 15,445 firms in 2024), not Amsterdam demand or national ride volume. Older city figure is 2,490 FIRMS in a 2022 overview, with 2020 population denominator; it is not 2,490 vehicles or a current fleet census. No credible market value or independently measured competitor share selected.

K2: Exclude the columnist’s 65% Uber estimate entirely from scoring; no disclosed method/source and TCA affiliation. The 80/16/4 ILT market split has no stated denominator and dates from the 2022 overview. ILT’s 57% refers to inspections, not share of trips.

K2: Operator and driver requirements and the street-hail/rank TTO system are supported. Current detailed Amsterdam TTO membership rules and Green SM’s actual licence/membership status are not established. Do not make a legal-compliance judgement about Green SM from absence of evidence.

K3: €4.31/€3.17/€0.52 are 2026 national maximum street-hail/rank charges, NOT Green SM fares. The €34.30 trip is an illustrative maximum-rate calculation. TCA is an advertised airport-route competitor price, and airport-origin pick-up has an extra €7.50. Neither is evidence of realised Green SM fare or average Amsterdam spend.

K3: One Media’s €8,500/100 panels/one week is indicative media inventory pricing only, excluding creative and printing. No committed group budget, confirmed inventory, robust digital CPM/CAC, campaign reach, conversion, repeat-rate or unit-economics benchmark. The contradictory 600-panel price is excluded.

K3 parent-owned sources: Green SM pilot promotion belongs to green-sm-2026a and is not duplicated. Full extracted text of parent-held green-and-smart-mobility-netherlands-b-v-ndb-green-sm-car.pdf was checked: p. 2 gives VAT/insurance and fare caveats; p. 3 gives up-to-30-day prebooking and cancellation before driver arrival. No numerical tariff was present in extracted text; this is NOT a claim that no fare is ever published or in the app. Parent owns visual/live verification and source integration.

K4: A positioning problem can be proposed from the electric incumbent offer and the need to distinguish customer value beyond another app, but that remains an analyst inference. The selected TCA-affiliated column is one interested opinion, not Dutch public sentiment. Parent-held company sources establish pilot status; no verified Green SM local users, paid rides, retention, revenue, stated numeric market objectives or app ratings selected.

K5: Correct the 2023 taxi zero-emission plan against January 2025 implementation reporting: scooters/vans/lorries were covered and taxis followed general passenger-car rules. Do not describe the historical proposal as an in-force taxi mandate or assert September 2026 legal certainty without the primary current municipal instrument. Uber’s electric premium option means “electric” alone is not demonstrated uniqueness.

K5: Digital 2026 was published 5 November 2025. National internet-user estimates and social-media identities support digital accessibility, not Amsterdam taxi-app adoption or AI/personalisation acceptance. No new marketing concept or outside framework is introduced by these sources.

K6: The documented story is a new Amsterdam pilot against established electric competition and prior VinFast Dutch retail-model change. Connecting the 2025 store closures with 2026 mobility expansion is explicitly an analyst interpretation, not proof of failure or consumer attitudes. No verified source supports “first Asian taxi company in Europe” or “first Vietnamese taxi in the Netherlands”. Group must select its own market; this manifest gives evidence, not a decision.

Metadata: Factsheet european-commission-2025b has no readable author field or PDF Author metadata; official European Commission provenance is corroborated by its companion annex. Flag for honest manual registry verification, not author substitution or lowered thresholds. Annex key european-commission-2025c is shared with Denmark; promote once. All entries remain candidate, no source marked cited.

K1: official 2026 population is a Census 2011-based projection for NCT of Delhi, not all NCR. Income is a secondary reported estimate, not household purchasing power. National TGM data cannot replace a current Delhi-NCR survey; Gupta/Sinha fieldwork is September–December 2021. No recent Delhi-NCR EV-cab willingness-to-pay research is established.

K2: Rapido/Uber/Ola figures are national app MAU estimates, not Delhi car-only shares or completed rides. Delhi-NCR market volume and serviceable market size remain missing. BluSmart is a historical suspended operator/insolvency case in these sources; no verified resumed operations.

Geography: reported service footprint spans NCT of Delhi, Gurugram in Haryana and selected Noida areas in Uttar Pradesh. Delhi population, academic sample and 2023 scheme are not interchangeable with NCR. Haryana/UP operational rules, later Delhi amendments and Green SM licensing compliance remain unchecked.

K3: current published Green SM India fare table, minimum/per-km/time charges, current promotion terms and method-disclosed India channel-cost benchmarks remain missing from this source set. INR 8/km is unconfirmed pre-launch speculation; INR 320/6.81 km is one pre-launch observed ride, not a tariff. No credible CPM/CPC/CAC or channel conversion benchmark is supplied.

Existing parent-owned green-sm-2026b-india-limo-launch.pdf was locally rechecked: physical p. 5 gives app/hotline/street-hail booking and a 50% promotion capped INR 250 for 5–11 June 2026. This is expired launch-offer evidence, not current pricing. No duplicate entry created; all Green SM browser work remains parent-owned.

K3/K4: 10,000 vehicles is an eventual company target; approximately 20% corporate and up to 33% airport are expected ride mix, not actual performance or necessarily over half. Company target horizon and current rides/users/retention are unverified. Driver guarantees are not marketing budget costs.

K4: premium-positioning/repeat-choice problem has reporting and a single review, not validated customer segmentation or causal price-sensitivity estimates. Driver payout allegations are limited paywall excerpts without accessible company reply; do not treat as established breach or prevalence.

K5: national EV adoption/charging infrastructure does not measure Delhi fleet charging access, operating economics or lifecycle emissions. Subscription is a reported future plan, not verified live product; corporate partnership is announced, not measured volume. AI/safety effectiveness and India personalisation/loyalty programmes remain unverified.
K6: launch and company-controlled EV story are documented, but no verified “first” claim. Do not describe BluSmart as currently operating or Green SM as already achieving proposed scale.

Access limits: TGM saved summary is not paid full report; Mint, Business Standard and Indian Express are partial articles with claim-bearing accessible body text. Their article page counts include paywall/navigation pages and must not be used as evidence depth.

Gupta/Sinha is empirical evidence, not permission to introduce LCCA/MaaS or another novel marketing framework. module_source truthfully records external empirical status, not that the paper or method was taught.

Names: Siddharth remains a printed single name; Sankunni K is preserved whole rather than treating K as an established surname; Surajeet Das Gupta keeps compound surname Das Gupta; BL Mumbai Bureau is corporate/byline authorship. Do not invent alternate author metadata to satisfy a verifier.
